subjects.displayTitle: Critiquing Eastern societies: dignity, renewal, and mutual learning
subjects.introduction: Iran was once a supreme paradise whose scholars taught the world, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes to a newspaper editor, and then describes without flinching how that light turned to darkness and the land fell from glory into abasement. Love for a society and severe judgment of it can live in the same sentence. He hopes the East will take from the West its material civilisation while giving back a divine one, and in the same breath urges Eastern peoples to guard their honour and frontiers from Western encroachment. His criticisms are pointed: statesmen who sell their country’s resources to fill their pockets, parties striking an axe at the root of an ancient edifice, religious conflict that poisons social life, and above all the imprisonment of women behind a veil never meant to bar them from learning. Much of this comes from reported conversations and carries the heat of its moment; it describes a situation, not the permanent nature of a people. The Qur’an ties human diversity to coming to know one another and measures honour by conduct rather than lineage [1], a fair test for any cultural criticism. The subject opens onto the meeting of East and West, the critique of Western values, the station of women, and the future of Iran, whose fresh saplings are expected to bear fruit.
subjects.arc: Begin with mutual learning and the protection of dignity, examine criticism in its historical settings, then turn toward education, equal rights, and renewal.

order.why: Explore the reported argument for women’s learning and participation.
shortened: The veil of women prevents education and learning.

Chastity is necessary and self-control is very important, but not to the degree that it prevents education and learning, for the Law of God establishes virtues - they should not be prevented from acquiring virtues.

order.why: Consider religious conflict as an obstacle to social life.
Open with the reported reciprocity of East and West.
Describes conflict and estrangement in the East and their transformation through teachings of unity.
Place protection from Western encroachment beside that exchange.
Read the editor’s address through the contrast of past achievement and present loss.
shortened: The people of Iran were at the forefront of knowledge and wisdom, and Iran's scholars were the educators and teachers of humankind. Its glory was enduring and the fame of its greatness was world-embracing. Its morals were the virtues of the human world and its ways were divine perfections.
But alas, that light turned to darkness, and the people of Iran fell into conflict with each other until they mixed with other peoples.
No trace of former virtues remained, and it fell from the heights of glory to the depths of abasement.

order.why: Keep sorrow over Iran’s condition tied to concern for its people.
Consider the practical invitation to learn from European institutions.
Introduce the image of fresh saplings and future growth.
Read the criticism of oppression and corruption.
Consider the paradox of rebuilding through destructive rivalry.
shortened: O ye who thirst for the truth!

Iran is in ruins; indeed, all parties have taken an axe in hand and are striking at the root of this ancient edifice, utterly unaware that this axe is destroying the foundation and these blows are uprooting it. Each party imagineth that it is engaged in construction and yet, as is stated in the Qur'an, "by their own hands they demolish their houses".

order.why: Keep the reported judgment on competing political experiments attributed.
shortened: The Persians have tested every system for the salvation of their country. In Government they tried absolutism for many ages, and finally they realized it did not work; then they tried constitutionalism; this also did not yield any result; then they organized various political parties, Democratic, Liberal, Conservative, Union and Progress Republican, etc., these parties also worked against each other and instead of bringing order out of confusion, they made confusion worse confounded, and hastened the ruination of Persia.

order.why: Read the reported critique of officeholders and private interest.
shortened: The thoughts of the statesmen of the East are atrophied. Their hearts are devoid of the love of the progress of the nation. Their ideas are petty and not sublime; selfish and not disinterested, local and not general. They think more of the advancement of their own interests than that of the country. They are not far-seeing patriots but inexperienced tyros. They sell the resources of their own country, if they realize they can fill their own pockets.

order.why: Retain the brief reported reference to a court story without inventing it.
Hear the reported anxiety over Asia’s position.
shortened: Asia is pressed from all sides and no matter toward what horizon she looks anxiously for a ray of hope so that she may be delivered from this death, she cannot see but threatening clouds.

order.why: Keep the reported Ottoman and Iranian observations in their setting.
Read the severe polemical language about leaders and parties as a situated criticism.
Distinguish the reported critique of practice from rejection of Islam’s origin.
Read the reported conversation with a consul as a historical exchange.
Keep the critique of fantastic tales in its reported context.
Consider the distinction between a spiritual heritage and present spiritual life.
Retain the severe description of Copts as attributed historical language.
Read the reported generalization about Arabs critically and in context.
shortened: The Arabs we met today were deprived of civilization, and yet they think they are not in need of civilization or knowledge. They never prefer others to themselves, while in reality they are in absolute need of civilization and education. When the people of Europe look at the Arabs, they say - and they are right - that the Arabs are entirely deprived of every kind of knowledge, but they themselves think they are independent.

order.why: Keep the reported account of nomads attributed, including the source omission.
shortened: The nomads are utterly destitute of the knowledge of God. They live an animalistic life and all their thoughts are centered upon their cows, goats and crops. When they come together they speak of nothing else save these things. They know nothing else. Nominally they are Moslems, but they are unaware of the ideals of Mohammed...

order.why: Consider the practical reported criticism of visiting customs.
Read the reported criticism of wealth devoted to display.
Retain the reported observation about the appreciation of art.
Consider music as a field of renewed cultural possibility.
Examine the connection between women’s conditions and contempt.
Read the reported linguistic example of the abasement of women.
Keep the reported comparison with captivity in its historical setting.
Hear the reported affirmation of emancipation.
Read the reported call for equal rights across religious communities.
Keep the sweeping reported claim about education attributed.
Consider the reported image of need mistaken for sufficiency.
Read the reported explanation of a journey to the West.
Keep the reported East–West contrast distinct from a population judgment.
Consider the reported educational effects of the Paris visit upon Eastern audiences.
Read the account of changing reputation against inherited Western prejudice.
shortened: The East is regarded in the eyes of the West as consisting of savage peoples, considered an inferior race, abased and detested. Now the power of the Most Great Name has so penetrated the very arteries and sinews of the Western world that in all regions of the earth, multitudes worship the Persians. Despite the manifestation of this mighty power, still the Persians remain heedless and absorbed in negligence.

order.why: Consider the relationship between a sacred homeland and its international reputation.
shortened: The utmost they can do is this: the Persians are laying the axe and adze unto the root of their own tree. For the Baha'is have so illumined Persia in the eyes of mankind that today a vast multitude from the seven climes reveres that land, inasmuch as the Sun of Truth hath risen from that horizon and it is the sacred homeland of His Holiness Baha'u'llah.

order.why: Keep the reported concern that conflict undermines that effort.
Read the reported anecdote about losing a spiritual opportunity.
shortened: Once Badri Pasha said in an address, 'Gentlemen, Westerners have taken everything from us: the sciences, the arts and the laws they took from the East. Now we fear that they may wrest from us the Cause of Baha'u'llah, as well.'

order.why: Hear the lament over prolonged imprisonment.
shortened: How foolish are the people of the East to have incarcerated for wellnigh fifty years the like of this glorious Personage!

order.why: Keep the concise criticism of heedlessness in its setting.
shortened: Praise be to God, notwithstanding this great gift (of the Cause) the Persians are captives of the neglectful sleep, and in relationship to this Cause they are ashamed and disgraced.

order.why: Read discord as a barrier to response.
Consider the image of a light recognized across distant lands.
Close with the call to awaken to a melody already being heard.

questions: How does opening with mutual learning change your reading of the severe criticisms that follow?
What concerns about oppression, education, public service, and dignity recur across the different settings?
How can we distinguish a historically situated criticism from an unjust generalization about a people?
What does Qur’an 49:13 contribute to an inquiry about cultural identity and the measure of human worth?
How do the passages on women and education connect renewal with the release of neglected capacities?
How would reading the connected critique of Western culture deepen or challenge your understanding of these selections?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 49:13 · Peoples, mutual knowledge, and conduct
references.note: In the Pickthall and Yusuf Ali translations, human diversity is associated with coming to know one another, while honor before God is connected with conduct or righteousness. Use this as a comparative question for reading historical cultural criticism: what enables criticism to serve mutual understanding and improvement without hardening into contempt?

subjects.displayTitle: Elections: freedom of conscience and responsibility for the whole
subjects.introduction: Elect with complete freedom, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá said when asked how members of a Spiritual Assembly should be chosen, and almost everything else about Bahá’í elections unfolds from that short answer. No tactics, no ambition; the person fit for office is the one who protests unworthiness. Shoghi Effendi draws the consequence: nomination and campaigning are discarded, because they endanger the elector’s freedom and breed parties, and in their place each believer is asked to stay in close and continued contact with fellow believers, and so to become an intelligent and responsible elector. The ballot is cast in private, in an atmosphere of prayer, with conscience the only limit, and the result is received as an expression of the will of God. Acts shows an early community choosing seven people of trusted character to meet a practical need, a comparison about service rather than procedure [1]. From here the road leads into the life of spiritual assemblies and the House of Justice, into the meaning of true liberty, and into the relationship between a people and its constitutional government.
subjects.arc: Begin with free choice and service, examine early institutional arrangements in context, then explore the later counsels on informed, prayerful, independent judgment.

order.why: Distinguish the reported discussion of a republic from Bahá’í internal elections.
Open with the direct affirmation of complete freedom in election.
Read the reported exclusion of tactics and personal ambition.
Consider the reported description of someone who does not seek rank.
shortened: The president must be a man who does not insistently seek the presidency. He should be a person free from all thoughts of name and rank; rather, he should say, 'I am unworthy and incapable of this position and cannot bear this great burden.' Such persons deserve the presidency.

order.why: Read sincerity and harmony alongside the reported early procedure.
shortened: The election should be carried out with sincerity and good will. People should be elected who when united together will give the most harmony.
Question: Is the method they use in Persia of appointing a committee of  selection which appoints the members of the House of Spirituality suitable  for America?
Abdul-Baha: "Yes, you should do the same."

order.why: Consider the participation of both women and men in assemblies.
Read the reported qualifications concerning character and law.
Keep the reported question about occasional participation in its original setting.
shortened: I asked if at time of an election many were brought in who seldom attend the meetings, in order to cast their votes, what shall we do?
He answered, "The members of the spiritual assembly must be well known and firm Baha'is. Those souls who come once in a while to the meetings are not Baha'is."

order.why: Explore the connection between general election and confidence in an assembly.
shortened: O ye beloved friends of 'Abdu'l-Baha! Should you observe that through a general election the Spiritual Assembly will gain increased influence and no one will have cause for objection or hesitation, and all will acknowledge the decisions of the Spiritual Assembly, in such case a general election would be better and more fitting.

order.why: Read the concise expectation of calm proceedings.
shortened: Consider how many election meetings are held in the world, how many great assemblies are established - no outcry, no clamor, no conflict and no disputation.

order.why: Keep the historical description of peaceful elections attributed.
Read calm and dignity in relation to actual slander and hostility.
Keep the condition concerning government authorization in context.
Read the postponement of procedures under particular political circumstances.
Retain the specific decision to continue an existing body.
shortened: It was observed that this commotion in Tehran would not subside unless the election was not renewed at this time. Therefore, the continuation of the previous body was cabled.

order.why: Keep the reply concerning the timing of Eastern delegates.
Examine the explicitly temporary assembly and its formation.
shortened: Therefore it appears that the Hands of the Cause, upon them be the Most Glorious Glory of God, and several wise and unbiased friends should gather and name eighty-one distinguished believers. Then divide those souls into groups of nine. Each group of nine should gradually gather in a location and elect one person. Then those nine elected ones should join with the Hands of the Cause to establish a Spiritual Assembly, and all the friends should obey and submit to that Assembly and serve it and strive to uphold its authority.
Thus in that Spiritual Assembly, which is a temporary body until the prescribed assembly is formed, the Hands of the Cause of God are permanent members.

order.why: Read the related statement concerning permanent and elected members.
Consider the specified indirect procedure in its historical setting.
Retain the arrangement for a smaller community.
shortened: [Regarding] the Spiritual Assembly of Ishqabad: You asked about the election of the Spiritual Assembly. In a city where the friends of God are few in number, every twenty, thirty, forty or fifty people, depending on whether there are fewer or more friends, should elect one person.

order.why: Keep the early five-year arrangement in its stated circumstances.
Read the further instruction about local rules and a five-year period.
Compare the reported early procedure and differing periods of office.
shortened: The friends elect a committee of, say, thirty-eight as a selection committee, and this committee appoints the spiritual assembly. Abdul Baha says that in the West both men and women should associate in the same assembly. Members are elected for periods of two and three years. All retire together at the end of the period of office and a new spiritual assembly is appointed in the same manner. Abdul Baha says that this method of election which is used in Persia should also be used in the West.

order.why: Retain the additional reported description of a committee.
Read the reported relationship of local and national bodies.
Keep the reported international arrangement distinct from later constitutional provisions.
Consider the reported analogy with congressional representation.
Read the statement of an all-embracing House of Justice.
Explains successive representative elections from local assemblies to the Supreme House of Justice.
Keep the reported choice of a center within institutional judgment.
Examine the specific directions about deputies and authorized action.
Read the conditions concerning membership, removal, and resignation.
Preserve the brief reported answer about replacing a member.
Consider consultation and a majority decision about a convention location.
Read the acceptance of a convention’s majority decision.
Keep the reported comparison between convention and House of Justice qualified.
Retain the isolated reported observation within its limited context.
Turn to the supplied constitutional statement of a prayerful atmosphere.
Read the supplied rejection of nomination and its reasons.
shortened: The practice of nomination being thus contrary to the spirit of Baha'i Administration should be totally discarded by all the friends. For otherwise the freedom of the Baha'i elector in choosing the members of any Baha'i Assembly will be seriously endangered leaving the way open for the domination of personalities. Not only that; but the mere act of nomination leads eventually to the formation of parties--a thing which is totally alien to the spirit of the Cause.

order.why: Consider the development of initiative and responsibility.
Connect informed choice with continued participation in community life.
shortened: To be able to make a wise choice at the election time, it is necessary for him to be in close and continued contact with all of his fellow -- believers, to keep in touch with local activities, be they teaching, administrative or otherwise, and to fully and whole-heartedly participate in the affairs of the local as well as national committees and Assemblies in his country. It is only in this way that a believer can develop a true social consciousness, and acquire a true sense of responsibility in matters affecting the interests of the Cause. Baha'i community life thus makes it a duty for every loyal land faithful believer to become an intelligent, well -- informed and responsible elector, and also gives him the opportunity of raising himself to such a station.

order.why: Distinguish acquaintance and discussion of qualifications from promotion of individuals.
Read preparation for election as a continuing duty.
Consider capacity, diversity, and the functions of the body.
Retain the supplied summary of qualifications and reflection.
Keep the supplied prohibition of canvassing with its visible omissions.
Read the successive supplied letters about civic participation in their separate historical settings.
shortened: Concerning the presidential elections, Shoghi Effendi says that we should avoid anything that would identify the Cause as a body with one party or the other. Any such recommendation on the part of the Assemblies, no matter how indirect it may be, will show that the Cause is favouring one party against another. It is for the friends individually and independently to study the issues and find to what party they desire to extend their support. Election should be free and not subjected to such influences. The friends should individually see what the proper course is and follow it.

(20 Aug. 1932 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi to Willard Hatch) Now, regarding the question of Baha'i participation in the presidential elections in America: the Guardian wishes me to state that he has never instructed any believer to refrain from voting, as he believes that this is essentially a question which involves the application of an administrative principle of the Cause; and as you well know the application of all such administrative principles is primarily the function of the Local and National Assemblies, and not of the Guardian. Shoghi Effendi has already restated the principle laid down by the Master namely that the believers should keep away from political activities. The task of determining what activity is political or not is that of the Assemblies, inasmuch as it constitutes the application of a Baha'i administrative principle, and not its formulation or its interpretation.

order.why: Conclude with the relationship between inward freedom and collective spiritual purpose.
shortened: Equally significant to the procedures for election -- to further extend the example -- is the evocation of that rarefied atmosphere of prayer and reflection, that quiet dignity of the process, devoid of nominations and campaigning, in which the individual's freedom to choose is limited only by his own conscience, exercised in private in an attitude that invites communion with the Holy Spirit. In this sphere, the elector regards the outcome as an expression of the will of God and those elected as being primarily responsible to that will, not to the constituency which elected them.

questions: What changes when an election is understood as an opportunity for service and the development of responsibility?
How can electors become well informed about one another while protecting freedom from nomination and campaigning?
What do the differences among early arrangements and later guidance teach about reading institutional history?
How does prayerful reflection relate to practical knowledge of the work an elected body must perform?
What similarities and differences appear when Acts 6 is read beside these passages?
How might freedom of individual judgment and concern for the whole strengthen each other?

references.label: 1 · Acts 6:1–6 · Choosing people to meet a community need
references.note: A dispute over the daily provision for widows leads the community to choose seven people of trusted reputation, wisdom, and spiritual qualities. Compare the attention to character, practical responsibilities, and prayer with the concerns here. The account offers a different institutional setting and does not establish the procedures of Bahá’í elections.

subjects.displayTitle: Speaking of others: attention, trust, and the life of a community
subjects.introduction: Speak ill of someone who is not in the room and the first casualty is the mood of those who heard you: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá names backbiting the leading cause of the friends drawing back from one another, a divisiveness that dampens zeal and quietly empties a community. Bahá’u’lláh forbids it in the same breath as murder and adultery, and says it quenches the light of the heart. Yet the remedy He proposes is not a tightened lip so much as a redirected gaze: busy yourself with your own faults, look for the perfections of others, and, like Christ before the dead dog, find the white teeth. The listener carries a share of the responsibility, and can turn a damaging story aside with courtesy. Truth is no defence; a fault truly described in someone’s absence is still backbiting. The Qur’an sets suspicion, spying and backbiting side by side, makes the injury vivid in a bodily image, and ends in mercy [1], which is also where change becomes possible. The road onward passes through silence and fewness of words, the golden rule and regard for one’s neighbour, and the difference between words and deeds.
subjects.arc: Begin with the effect upon a community, turn toward self-examination and appreciative attention, then consider listening, truthful speech, and constructive action.

order.why: Connect speech about others with the seeker’s inward life.
shortened: That seeker should also regard backbiting as grievous error, and keep himself aloof from its dominion, inasmuch as backbiting quencheth the light of the heart, and extinguisheth the life of the soul.

order.why: Open with the effect of backbiting on participation and the listener’s responsibility.
shortened: O beloved of the Lord! If any soul speak ill of an absent one, the only result will clearly be this: he will dampen the zeal of the friends and tend to make them indifferent. For backbiting is divisive, it is the leading cause among the friends of a disposition to withdraw. If any individual should speak ill of one who is absent, it is incumbent on his hearers, in a spiritual and friendly manner, to stop him, and say in effect: would this detraction serve any useful purpose?

order.why: Identifies praise and love of the friends with firmness in the Covenant and contrasts them with backbiting.
Trace the reported growth of a story into division.
Read the loss of love through mutual denunciation.
Consider the spread of a harmful conversational habit.
shortened: Furthermore, some had secretly begun to speak ill of others without cause, and these individuals gradually increased in number and were daily multiplying. It was observed that if this situation were to continue in this manner, this condition would spread to all, and in this manifest Day such a state must not and should not exist.

order.why: Turn attention toward one’s own faults and reciprocity.
Read the purpose of the tongue and the discipline of attention.
Read the explicit prohibition in the Aqdas.
Retain the concise restatement of the ordinance.
shortened: Say: Beware lest ye backbite one another. This is what We have forbidden in the laws and ordinances.

order.why: Hear the short direct warning.
shortened: Say: Sanctify yourselves from that which kindleth the fire. Beware lest ye backbite one another. Be as brothers seated on thrones, facing one another.

order.why: Read the counsel concerning reviling and attention.
Keep the reported parallel attributed.
Retain the particular instruction to cleanse speech.
Connect restraint with the positive adornment of love and fellowship.
Read forgiveness and the possibility of a new pattern of speech.
Consider the effect of words upon another person’s grief.
Encounter the story of Christ noticing the dead dog’s teeth.
shortened: One day, Jesus son of Mary - may my spirit be sacrificed for Him - was walking with several of His disciples when they came upon a dead dog. They expressed disgust, saying they detected a foul odor. That Source of compassion and mercy said, "How white are its teeth!" Observe now how He concealed the fault - may my spirit be sacrificed for His loving-kindness. This was solely to teach His companions that all should fix their gaze upon the good deeds of others and conceal one another's faults. We bear witness that He is verily the All-Knowing, the Wise Teacher.

order.why: Read the fuller counsel on seeking perfections.
shortened: I hope that the divine friends will become completely averse to backbiting and each will praise the other, and know backbiting to be the cause of divine retribution, reaching such a degree that if anyone speaks a word of backbiting they become disgraced among all the friends. For fault-finding is the most detestable characteristic. One must seek to discover the praises of souls, not investigate people's faults. As much as possible, one must overlook faults and discuss people's perfections, not their deficiencies.

order.why: Consider the reported invitation to find virtues in every person.
Keep the reported image of a sin-covering eye.
shortened: Admonish the Friends so they will not backbite and criticize, voicing the mistakes and sins of others. Have a sin-covering eye.

order.why: Explore the reported connection between fault-finding and conceit.
Read the reported questions that redirect scrutiny toward oneself.
Retain the reported challenge to hypocrisy.
shortened: Heedless souls are always seeking faults in others. What can the hypocrite know of others' faults when he is blind to his own?

order.why: Keep the severe moral language in its attributed form.
Read the range of people included in the instruction.
shortened: Never has it been permissible for anyone to speak critically of another, even if they be among the wicked - how much less so for the righteous, even if they be strangers - how much less so for loved ones and the virtuous.

order.why: Notice that allusion and suggestion can also injure.
shortened: And as for other matters, my advice to you is not to mention anyone negatively, even by allusion or suggestion.

order.why: Consider the responsibility to discourage an entrenched habit.
shortened: You must certainly exercise the utmost vigilance and explicitly forbid everyone from this, for no habit is more harmful than this trait of fault-finding, especially in relation to the Cause of God. Never should anyone express a word or hint that is unworthy about any of the friends of God. How strange that one should be occupied with the faults of others while heedless of his own faults! This is the path of the spiritual ones. Exercise the utmost care in preventing this habit and never allow anyone to utter anything except praise.

order.why: Read the reported courteous refusal to hear detraction.
Keep the reported boundary set against private complaints.
Retain the source summary of counsel to a listener.
Consider timing and audience even when speaking of good things.
Read the reported conjunction of honesty, investigation, humility, and gentleness.
shortened: Above all other things we must be honest to our consciences and not dissimulate. We must not speak against each other either publicly or privately. We must not belittle the services rendered by others because they are not so fortunately situated as ourselves. We must be humble. We must not have the spirit of destructive criticism. Before making any statement we must investigate it well, whether it is true or not. We must not make the hearts of other people sad. We must speak with gentleness and brotherliness. We must not backbite.

order.why: Keep the warning about repeating what has not been witnessed.
Consider the invitation to turn from suspicion toward assurance.
shortened: How then could it be that the friends of God would plot against you? Hold fast unto the manifest certitude, turning away from idle fancies and vain imaginings."

order.why: Read the contrast between certitude and idle fancies.
shortened: Blessed art thou for having cast aside idle fancies and taken hold of that which hath been revealed from God, the Lord of the seen and unseen.
By God's life! The ocean of certitude hath surged before the faces of men, yet they hasten toward idle fancies.

order.why: Retain the wider warning about suppositions in its religious setting.
Keep the reported counsel about silence toward wrongdoers.
shortened: There are many bad people in the world; have nothing to do with them. Do not gossip about them. It must be so that your very silence should be blame (reproof?) itself.

order.why: Read the further reported version with its own wording.
Explore the reported link between excessive speech and desire for fame.
shortened: People speak too much because they seek fame, because they wish to be thought better than their brethren. Those who do most good say the least about it.

order.why: Consider the loss of time through vain talk.
Read the reported burden of listening patiently to unprofitable talk.
shortened: Profitless discussions fatigue and weary a person. People who call on me almost every day carry on a stream of profitless, unspiritual talk and I must listen to them with patience.

order.why: Turn toward purposeful learning and conversation.
shortened: "Now, if you occupy yourselves, for instance, in affirming some reasons for the truth of this holy Cause and how to deliver the Word of God to everyone, these things will support and strengthen you and will prepare you for the good of this world and that which is to come; but if, God forbid, you lose your time in vain chattering and useless talk and running hither and thither, these things, be sure, will never lead you to the way of salvation.

order.why: Read the supplied definition and insistence that factual truth alone is insufficient.
shortened: As regards backbiting, i.e. discussing the faults of others in their absence, the teachings are very emphatic.
Even if what is said against another person be true, the mentioning of his faults to others still comes under the category of backbiting, and is forbidden."

order.why: Consider the supplied counsel on forgiveness, sincerity, and gentle admonition.
shortened: You must not see evil as evil and then compromise with your opinion, for to treat in a smooth, kindly way one whom you consider evil or an enemy is hypocrisy, and this is not worthy or allowable. You must consider your enemies as your friends, look upon your evil-wishers as your well-wishers and treat them accordingly. Act in such a way that your heart may be free from hatred. Let not your heart be offended with anyone. If some one commits an error and wrong toward you, you must instantly forgive him. Do not complain of others. Refrain from reprimanding them, and if you wish to give admonition or advice, let it be offered in such a way that it will not burden the bearer.

order.why: Close with the supplied image of attending to one’s own furrow and living the teachings.
shortened: We are like ploughmen each of whom has his team to manage and his plough to direct, and in order to keep his furrow straight he must keep his eye on his goal and concentrate on his own task. If he looks to this side and that to see how Tom and Harry are getting on and to criticize their ploughing, then his own furrow will assuredly become crooked. On no subject are the Baha'i teachings more emphatic than on the necessity to abstain from faultfinding and backbiting while being ever eager to discover and root out our own faults and overcome our own failings. If we profess loyalty to Baha'u'llah, to our Beloved Master and our dear Guardian, then we must show our love by obedience to these explicit teachings. Deeds not words are what they demand, and no amount of fervour in the use of expressions of loyalty and adulation will compensate for failure to live in the spirit of the teachings.

questions: How can speech about an absent person affect a community’s trust and willingness to participate?
What is the difference between seeking another person’s good qualities and offering praise one does not mean?
How might a listener redirect a damaging conversation with both firmness and kindness?
What connections does Qur’an 49:12 suggest among suspicion, intrusion, speech, and mercy?
What considerations distinguish idle detraction from truthful communication needed to address harm or fulfill a responsibility?
How could the golden rule and the relationship between words and deeds change an ordinary conversation this week?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 49:12 · Suspicion, backbiting, and mercy
references.note: Compare the Pickthall and Arberry translations. The verse joins warnings against suspicion, spying, and backbiting, using a disturbing bodily image to make the injury vivid, then closes with divine mercy. Read it alongside the images of extinguished light and damaged fellowship here, asking how an inward habit becomes a social harm and how change remains possible.

subjects.displayTitle: Study and deepening: from the page into a life
subjects.introduction: Immerse yourselves in the ocean of My words, Bahá’u’lláh says, that you may discover the pearls hidden in its depths; and blessed, He adds, is the one who reads and then ponders. Deepening begins in that second verb. It is the return to familiar words with the patience of a pupil who learns by persisting, and it refuses to be satisfied with words when the spiritual meaning is what matters. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá sends inquirers to particular books, the Íqán, the Hidden Words, and urges wider learning in science, philosophy and the scriptures of other faiths, while Shoghi Effendi insists that study anchor itself in the actual words of Bahá’u’lláh and the Master yet leave freedom to explain how they bear on a life. Confucius warned that learning without thought is lost and thought without learning perilous [1], a reciprocity echoed here. Study also corrects: further reading exposes earlier errors, and the community becomes the laboratory in which principles are tested by action. The path continues into the daily reading of the Sacred Writings, the practice of contemplation, the call to acquire knowledge, and the discipline of rational argument.
subjects.arc: Enter through the ocean of words, develop habits of reading and reflection, then connect disciplined understanding with service, revision, and shared life.

order.why: Open with the ocean and its undiscovered pearls.
shortened: Immerse yourselves in the ocean of My words, that ye may unravel its secrets, and discover all the pearls of wisdom that lie hid in its depths. Take heed that ye do not vacillate in your determination to embrace the truth of this Cause--a Cause through which the potentialities of the might of God have been revealed, and His sovereignty established.

order.why: Read the blessing of reading joined to pondering.
shortened: Blessed is he who readeth the verses of God and pondereth upon the pearls of his Lord's knowledge that lie concealed therein, the Mighty, the All-Knowing.

order.why: Extend the image through the invitation to a seeker.
shortened: O thou who art seeking after Knowledge!  Immerse thyself in the ocean of the explanation of the Beauty of the Merciful, so that thou mayest gather the pearls.

order.why: Consider the reported distinction between words and their spiritual meanings.
Read study, listening, thought, and understanding together.
Consider the reported patience of a beginner.
Explore the concrete guidance about books and translations.
shortened: Thou didst ask as to acquiring knowledge: read thou the Books and Tablets of God, and the articles written to demonstrate the truth of this Faith. Included among them are the Iqan, which hath been translated into English, the works of Mirza Abu'l-Fadl, and those of some others among the believers. In the days to come a great number of holy Tablets and other sacred writings will be translated, and thou shouldst read these as well.

order.why: Read the reported account of fundamental works.
Consider gathering and reading Tablets for steadfastness.
Read the request to obtain and study sacred books.
shortened: Sacred Books have been sent down from the heaven of God's Will - request them from the loved ones and study them, that ye may become aware of the greatness of this Cause and arise to exalt the Word of God.

order.why: Keep the reported invitation to study the Hidden Words.
shortened: Read the Tablets of Baha'u'llah. Study the hidden words. Then thou wilt become spiritual, illumined, godlike, divine.

order.why: Retain the reported call to familiarity, including the source omission.
shortened: They must always read the holy books, so that they may be familiar with their contents...

order.why: Read the reported invitation to understand the Hebrew and Christian scriptures.
Encounter the reported consolation found in reading the Qur’an.
Connect youthful study with understanding and convincing evidence.
Encourages proper study to gain knowledge and explain the verses of divine books to others.
Read the reported practice of reviewing proofs together.
shortened: When you, who are the believers of God gather together in a meeting, let all your conversation be about the Cause, review the proofs that uphold it, bring forth the evidence that reinforces it and investigate the arguments that demonstrate it.

order.why: Consider the growth of proficiency and understanding.
Read the reported difference between firsthand learning and hearsay.
shortened: In these gatherings where we have met and spoken together you have all become acquainted with the principles of this dispensation, and with the reality of facts. Unto you it has been given to know these things, but there are many still unenlightened and submerged in superstition. They have heard but little of this great and glorious Cause, and the knowledge they have is for the most part based only on hearsay.

order.why: Connect reported enlightenment with guidance and service.
shortened: We must endeavor to gain heavenly enlightenment, to understand the mysteries of the holy books, to become the cause of guidance to others and to illumine hearts.

order.why: Consider reading aloud and memorizing particular passages.
shortened: You are to explain to them or read to them the Ishrakat, Tarazat, Tajalleyat, the Words of Paradise, and Tablet of the World. You have to make them learn by heart some of these verses.

order.why: Read the etiquette of attentive listening and courteous speech.
shortened: Those souls who are in that assembly before their entrance therein must be adorned with utmost purity, turn their faces toward the Kingdom of ABHa and enter with infinite humility and meekness, and when someone reads Tablets they must be silent and attentive. Should anyone desire to speak, he must do it with the utmost courtesy and with perfect eloquence and fluency by the consent and permission of the people of the assembly.

order.why: Keep the small-group directions within their circumstances of danger.
shortened: The friends in every land should gather together with wisdom and utterance in meetings and assemblies to read the verses of God, for the verses kindle the fire of love and ignite its flame. However, they must observe wisdom in all conditions, and gatherings of five to nine persons are sufficient. The locations must also be varied, for if they are held in one place, the heedless will become aware and cause commotion.

order.why: Consider the purposes of conversation in the gathering.
shortened: They must either teach or open their tongue in propounding arguments, either commune or supplicate and pray to God, either read Tablets or give out advices and exhortations.

order.why: Hear the reported joy of learning the history and teachings.
shortened: Every conversation, when it goes on too long, brings weariness to a person except conversation about the Divine Cause, conversation about the Exalted One [the Bab], about the Blessed Beauty [Baha'u'llah], about the beginning of this Cause, about the details of this Cause, about the proofs of this Cause, about the glad tidings of this Cause, about the events of the martyrs - how much joy these bring to a person.

order.why: Read the call to share the Book with receptive listeners.
shortened: Take thou the Book with a strength from Us, then read it unto those multitudes whom the affairs of the world have not kept back from the Ancient of Days, and whom the hosts of those who were heedless of this mighty Cause have not frightened.

order.why: Join remembrance of counsels with their embodiment.
shortened: You should remind all the loved ones of the divine counsels that have been revealed in the Sacred Books in this Most Great Revelation, that all may be adorned with the ornament of His favor and become the cause of remembrance among the peoples of the world.

order.why: Retain the personal invitation to the school of realities.
Read the particular commitment to learning and language study.
shortened: His honor Mirza Ali-Muhammad returned with a firm covenant and strong testament and faith and pledge that he would in no way deviate from your good pleasure, and would be occupied day and night with learning the lesson of teaching and studying the French language.

order.why: Connect character, sciences, arts, and teaching.
Keep the specific counsel to complete scientific studies.
shortened: Finish thy studies in sciences and then turn thy face unto God, asking from Him help and protection under all conditions.

order.why: Consider the reported encouragement of science, art, and literature.
Read the reported contrast of acquired learning and divine confirmation.
Retain the brief conditional counsel without supplying its unstated antecedent.
Read earnest study as a path toward living the faith.
shortened: I counsel you that you study earnestly the teachings of Baha'u'llah, so that, God helping you, you may in deed and truth become Baha'is.

order.why: Close the linked sequence with action as thanksgiving.
shortened: Therefore, in thanksgiving for them ye must act in accordance with the teachings of Baha'u'llah. Ye must read the Tablets -- the Hidden Words, Ishraqat, Glad Tidings -- all the holy utterances, and act according to them. This is real thanksgiving, to live in accord with these utterances.

order.why: Read the supplied invitation to selfless, concentrated attention.
Consider study that revises previous notions.
Keep fidelity to the words alongside freedom to explain their significance.
shortened: Surely the ideal way of teaching is to prove our points by constant reference to the actual words of Baha'u'llah and the Master.

This, however, does not mean that our freedom of expression is limited. We can always find new ways of approach to that truth or explain how they influence our life and condition. The more deep our studies the more we can understand the significance of the teachings. In the Cause we cannot divorce the letter from the spirit of the words. As Baha'u'llah says we should take the outward significance and superimpose upon it the inner. Either without the other is wrong and defective.

order.why: Explore the supplied relation to philosophy and science.
Read the value of broad learning in widening understanding.
Consider continuing study alongside other disciplines.
Keep the supplied counsel concerning writing, memory, and love.
Read the supplied distinction between study and excessive speculation.
shortened: Regarding your question concerning a deep and profound study of the teachings: of course the Baha'is can and should meditate upon the significances of the writings, and endeavour to grasp their meaning to the utmost.... However certain things are, by their very nature, a mystery to us, at least in our present stage of development.

The Guardian feels that, while there is no harm in speculation on these abstract matters, one should not attach too much importance to them. Science itself is far from having resolved the question of the nature of matter, and we cannot, in this physical world, grasp the spiritual one more than in a very fragmentary and inadequate manner.

order.why: Consider finite understanding and the continuing duty to learn.
Read the large questions posed for regular study.
shortened: What is Baha'u'llah's purpose for the human race? For what ends did He submit to the appalling cruelties and indignities heaped upon Him? What does He mean by "a new race of men"? What are the profound changes which He will bring about? The answers are to be found in the Sacred Writings of our Faith and in their interpretation by 'Abdu'l-Baha and our beloved Guardian. Let the friends immerse themselves in this ocean, let them organize regular study classes for its constant consideration, and, as reinforcement to their effort, let them remember conscientiously the requirements of daily prayer and reading of the Word of God enjoined upon all Baha'is by Baha'u'llah.

order.why: Keep the supplied historical appeal concerning the Covenant and institutions.
Connect spiritual understanding with the foundations of community institutions.
Read the supplied movement from study to transformed character.
Conclude with community life as a setting for learning through action.
shortened: The Baha'i community life provides you with an indispensable laboratory, where you can translate into living and constructive action the principles which you imbibe from the Teachings. By becoming a real part of that living organism you can catch the real spirit which runs throughout the Baha'i Teachings. To study the principles, and to try to live according to them, are, therefore, the two essential mediums through which you can ensure the development and progress of your inner spiritual life and of your outer existence as well.

questions: What habits help a familiar passage yield a fresh understanding?
How do reading, reflection, memory, prayer, and conversation contribute differently to learning?
What does the Analects’ pairing of learning and thought illuminate about these counsels?
How can wider study of science, philosophy, and other scriptures enrich understanding while keeping an author’s own words in view?
What might show that further study has corrected one of our earlier assumptions?
How could a group connect its next period of study with action and reflection in community life?

references.label: 1 · Confucius, Analects 2.15 · Learning and reflection
references.note: In James Legge’s translation, find the short saying in Part 2 that warns against separating learning from thought or thought from learning. Compare that reciprocal discipline with the calls here to read carefully, ponder meanings, examine arguments, and act. The traditions give these practices different spiritual and educational settings, while both invite more than passive accumulation of words.

subjects.displayTitle: The apostles: ordinary lives and an enduring influence
subjects.introduction: One seed became a harvest and one drop an ocean: that is how ‘Abdu’l-Bahá sums up what happened to a handful of fishermen and dyers with no name, no helper and no schooling. The apostles matter because they were ordinary, and because something made them otherwise. Peter and John, He says, were simple workmen until the Holy Spirit illumined them; men absorbed in their own advantage became just, self-sacrificing, alive while learned Herod and educated Pilate were dead. The onlookers in Acts, startled by the boldness of two unlettered men, could only conclude that they had been with Jesus [1]. After the crucifixion comes the part easiest to forget: shaken disciples consulting together, a pact to go out in different directions, provision made for families, Mary Magdalene steadying the others, and then homeless years on roads and in strange towns. Fidelity, not visible success, is the measure, and it asks what a faithful response could make possible in a life that looks unremarkable from outside. The way leads back to Christ and the beginnings of Christianity, and into the stories and anecdotes through which such examples travel.
subjects.arc: Begin with overlooked people transformed, follow the movement from grief to common purpose, then consider steadfast service and influence recognized over time.

order.why: Open with a seed becoming a harvest and a drop an ocean.
shortened: Consider how the disciples were few in number and had no helper or supporter, yet how heavenly blessings descended - one seed became a harvest and one drop became an ocean.

order.why: Read the transformation of ordinary occupations into spiritual influence.
Consider the reported account of Peter and John’s illumination.
shortened: The two great apostles, St Peter and St John the Evangelist, were once simple, humble workmen, toiling for their daily bread. By the Power of the Holy Spirit their souls were illumined, and they received the eternal blessings of the Lord Christ.

order.why: Explore the reported change of character through following Christ.
shortened: The apostles, who were the disciples of Jesus Christ, were just as other men are; they, like their fellows, were attracted by the things of the world, and each thought only of his own advantage. They knew little of justice, nor were the Divine perfections found in their midst. But when they followed Christ and believed in Him, their ignorance gave place to understanding, cruelty was changed to justice, falsehood to truth, darkness into light. They had been worldly, they became spiritual and divine.

order.why: Read the contrast between low public standing and lasting greatness.
Keep the reported mockery of fishermen in its setting.
shortened: In the time of Christ, outwardly the acceptance of the disciples had no importance - people mocked them, saying "What station or worth do fishermen have?"

order.why: Hear the reported wonder at the station attained.
shortened: Observe what blessed souls were raised up under the shadow of Christ - poor people and fishermen reached such stations!

order.why: Consider the reported transformation of weakness into strength.
shortened: Likewise, the disciples were the weakest souls, but through the Breath of the Holy Spirit and the assistance of the Kingdom of God, they became the strongest ones.

order.why: Keep the reported contrast with Herod and Pilate as spiritual rhetoric.
shortened: The disciples of Christ, though they were lacking in culture, were alive. But Herod was a learned man; nevertheless he was dead. Pilate was a highly educated man, but he was as dead.

order.why: Read the relation between detachment and an enduring light.
shortened: On the other hand, consider the Apostles of Christ! Although outwardly they were fishermen, yet because they renounced this world, opened their eyes to the Divine Universe, forgot entirely their personal selves, dedicated their lives to the Light of the world and became self-sacrificing in the path of His Holiness Christ - may my life be a ransom to Him! - these fishermen today are shining and gleaming with the light of God from the horizon of Eternity.

order.why: Consider awakening as the condition of radiance.
Read the reported image of Christ’s light reflected in other mirrors.
shortened: The focus of the rays of the Sun of Reality was Christ; and from this glorious focus the bounty of God was reflected upon the other mirrors which were the reality of the apostles...

order.why: Name Peter, Andrew, John, and Mary Magdalene together.
Recounts the disciples’ disturbance after Christ’s death and Mary Magdalene’s role in restoring their firmness.
Read the role of people who were not formally teachers.
Consider the reported account of Mary Magdalene strengthening disciples.
shortened: Remember that Peter was a fisherman, but through the bounty of the Kingdom he became the great apostle. Mary Magdalene was a villager of lowly type, yet that selfsame Mary was transformed and became the means through which the confirmation of God descended upon the disciples.

order.why: Read the further reported account of her influence.
Keep the reported beginning of her encouragement within its limited excerpt.
Follow the reported movement from shaken faith to responsibility.
shortened: Although after the crucifixion of His Holiness Christ, the apostles were shaken, yet soon they were awakened to the realization of their responsibilities and made aware of the character of their positions. They became as firm and steadfast as the rock. Then they arose to illuminate the lamp of the lost Cause and straighten the path of the Kingdom. They forgot everything and were filled with Christ.

order.why: Read Pentecost through spiritual triumph and confirmation.
shortened: The spirituality of Christ triumphed and the love of God took hold. On that day they received divine confirmations, and each departed in a different direction to teach the Cause of God and unloosed his tongue to set forth the proofs and testimonies.

order.why: Consider the reported question at the heart of consultation.
shortened: The most memorable instance of spiritual consultation was the meeting of the disciples of Jesus Christ upon the mount after His ascension. They said, "Jesus Christ has been crucified, and we have no longer association and intercourse with Him in His physical body; therefore, we must be loyal and faithful to Him, we must be grateful and appreciate Him, for He has raised us from the dead, He made us wise, He has given us eternal life. What shall we do to be faithful to Him?"

order.why: Read the reported meeting, covenant, and departure in different directions.
shortened: After the departure of His Holiness to the Supreme Paradise, the disciples who had followed His teachings met together in consultation upon the summit of a mountain near Jaffa.
Then they took an oath and covenant among themselves, embraced each other and descended from the mountain, some going to the Eastward, some to the West, North and South.

order.why: Keep the reported commitments and attention to family provision.
Read the further reported account of a shared pact.
Consider the reported lasting effects of that gathering.
shortened: All that hath since been effected along the line of diffusing the holy fragrances of Christ, uplifting the Word of God, spreading the Gospel, training souls and guiding the people, hath been wholly from the result of the effects produced by that assemblage of the disciples. Those effects are continual even in the present time.

order.why: Hear the reported fidelity expressed through remembering and striving.
shortened: They did not forget Christ, did not forget those favors, did not erase those teachings from view, did not forget His counsels and bounties. Night and day they strove that perhaps they might succeed. In truth, they showed the utmost faithfulness to Christ.

order.why: Read the reported combination of spiritual qualities and effort.
Consider the reported embodiment of mercifulness.
Read the reported daily hardships of travel and proclamation.
Keep the reported accounts of distant journeys attributed.
shortened: For example, with what self-sacrifice did the apostles of Christ arise to serve - they truly proved faithful to Christ. One went toward Iran and was completely lost. Another went toward India and he too was lost.

order.why: Retain the named examples of suffering in their source wording.
shortened: Remember the hardships of the disciples, and what Mary, the Virgin; Mary, the Magdalene; and Mary, the mother of Jesus, bore in the path of God; especially Barbara, until she was martyred in the love of Christ; and she being attracted unto the Kingdom of God, her spirit soared unto the summits of holiness in the paradise of eternal life, in the place of Meeting.

order.why: Consider the effect attributed to teachers enduring difficulty.
shortened: The state of Christ's apostles is known - when teachers live in utmost difficulty, it has a profound effect on seeking souls.

order.why: Read the reported importance of steadfastness after Christ’s departure.
Retain the further reported version amid overwhelming tests.
Consider the reported appeal to later believers through the apostles’ example.
shortened: After His Holiness Christ His apostles did not rest for one moment and devoted all their energies to the promotion of the Gospel of Salvation. With what greater enthusiasm and sincerity should we serve at the Threshold of Baha'u'llah. If the Apostles did not manifest that Superhuman steadfastness the Cause of Christ would have been disappeared entirely from the face of the earth in its beginning.

order.why: Keep the reported emphasis on devoted time and effort.
Read the direct invitation to follow an example of travel and service.
Hear the concise reported summons to arise.
shortened: Arise ye in service to the Cause of God as the Apostles arose after the departure of Christ.

order.why: Keep the statement of twelve luminous disciples in its setting.
Read the reported image of a table attended by eleven.
shortened: Thus Christ spread the table of his spiritual food and called a great number of people in order to take their portions. Out of these only eleven came and attended the table.

order.why: Retain the reported account of eleven disciples’ influence.
shortened: The results of these persecutions were eleven disciples who were truly blessed souls. They became luminous and heavenly; they became the cause of the enlightenment of the people of the world.

order.why: Consider the reported contrast between shaken beginnings and results.
shortened: After the departure of His Holiness Christ there were only eleven disciples whose faith was shaken and outwardly they were of the low class, deprived of any social distinctions! Now behold the results of their work.

order.why: Read the particular comparison with Budapest without turning it into a numerical measure of worth.
shortened: In the days of Christ, eleven souls were attracted through the power of the Holy Spirit, but in nine days blessed souls in Budapest entered the Abha Kingdom.

order.why: Keep the reported contrast of social standing in its historical religious setting.
Retain the incomplete narrative beginning without extending its generalization.
Read the selected beginning of the dead-dog story without supplying missing words.
Keep the skeptical claim in view as a claim rejected by its surrounding source, not as the speaker’s conclusion.
Consider the reported reverence even for places associated with the apostles.
Read the delayed recognition of their station.
shortened: Consider ye! In the day of His Highness Christ, the grandeur and majesty of their Holiness the Apostles, was not known. After three-hundred years the loftiness of the station and the exaltation of their attainment became manifest.

order.why: Return to the image of stars still shining.
shortened: How few were Christ's apostles, and they were in utmost abasement and lowliness in Jerusalem. Then observe what glory and greatness they attained, such that to this day they shine like stars from the horizon of sanctity.

order.why: Close with influence crossing East and West through the Holy Spirit.
shortened: Thou observest how the apostles and followers of Christ ultimately achieved victory and triumph, illumining East and West through the Holy Spirit.

questions: What changes of character make the apostles’ transformation significant in these passages?
How does the comparison with Acts 4:13 challenge familiar assumptions about who can contribute?
What roles do consultation, encouragement, and Mary Magdalene’s example play after a community experiences loss?
How can careful attention to the setting of a reported story prevent a quotation from being misunderstood?
What distinguishes fidelity and sustained service from a wish for immediate recognition or visible success?
Which aspect of these ordinary lives could illuminate a responsibility you or your community now face?

references.label: 1 · Acts 4:13 · Unexpected boldness
references.note: The observers are surprised by Peter and John’s boldness in view of their lack of recognized learning, and associate them with Jesus. Compare this moment with the compilation’s repeated contrast between outward standing and spiritual capacity. The verse supports an inquiry into transformation and recognition; it does not independently verify all the later stories about the apostles.

subjects.displayTitle: The journey to Constantinople: exile, service, and unexpected openings
subjects.introduction: In the garden of the house in Constantinople a single rose opened after sunset, out of season, and the exiles who had never seen a rose at that time of year gathered round it in delight. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s memory of that evening is a reminder that a banishment is lived through meals and saddles, tents pitched at nightfall and companions too tired to move, as much as through decrees. The Sháh of Persia, alarmed that pilgrims returning from Baghdad were becoming Bahá’ís, pressed the Ottoman court until an order came, phrased with utmost respect, that Bahá’u’lláh should grace Istanbul with His presence. He left Baghdad with a majesty that astonished the officials who came to bid Him farewell, crossed to the sea, and lived four months in the capital, seeking no one’s favour, before a further exile. Bahá’u’lláh protested the injustice plainly, and the suffering imposed is never softened. Paul, writing from confinement that his chains had served to advance the Gospel, offers a comparison for the way exile kept opening new ground to the message [1], without making the persecution anything but wrong. The path leads to the Declaration in the garden of Riḍván, the person of Bahá’u’lláh, and the whole course of His banishments.
subjects.arc: Begin with a small moment of joy, follow departure and the work of the journey, then explore dignity, protest, and the wider effects of exile.

order.why: Open with the reported rose and the community gathered around it.
Read the reported joy upon arrival as a question to explore.
Describes the circumstances of exile to Constantinople and the respect shown along the route.
Establish the stated political reason for removal from Baghdad.
Hear the direct protest concerning successive exiles.
shortened: In the name of God and humanity we protest to you against the plight which we have been subjected to from the Turkish government.  Six years ago we were invited at the Ottoman suggestion and we have accepted.  Later, without having committed any fault and at the request of Persia we were sent from Baghdad to Constantinople.  After a stay of four months, we were exiled to Adrianople.

order.why: Read the fuller reported account of negotiations and fears.
shortened: Communications passed between Tehran and the Iranian Foreign Ministry and the Ottoman Ministry, until finally Nasiri'd-Din Shah himself wrote to the Ottoman Sultan that his realm was in danger, and Baghdad being adjacent to Iran, his request was that they seize the Baha'is and hand them over to the governor of Kermanshah, 'Imadu'd-Dawlih, who would come with an army and take custody of them at the frontier. The Ottoman government did not accept this request. Nasiri'd-Din Shah's second request was that at least they be removed far from the Iranian border, that they not be near the Iranian frontier, as two hundred thousand pilgrims go to Baghdad yearly and many of them become Baha'is, therefore his request was that they move the Blessed Beauty from Baghdad. Thus came the Ottoman decree, with utmost respect, that circumstances required that He grace Istanbul with His presence. This is the basis of the migration of the Blessed Beauty from Baghdad to Istanbul.

order.why: Keep the reported compressed account of expulsion in its source form.
shortened: The government of Persia said: "As long as Baha'u'llah is in Persia the country will not be at peace. When Baha'u'llah is exiled from Persia the country will then find peace. He shall no longer be connected with this country; all communications with him shall be suspended." So the Shah of Persia endeavored until he succeeded in expelling the Blessed Perfection to Constantinople to Roumelia.

order.why: Consider the reported hostility of the Persian ambassador.
shortened: When we were exiled to Constantinople from Baghdad, the Persian Ambassador at the former city did his best to bring about our total destruction.

order.why: Read the reported orders and preparations for departure.
Hear the reported grief when the decree became known.
shortened: Having received the Firman of exile from Bagdad to Constantinople - when the friends heard this dire news their hearts were torn to pieces. Through the intensity of anguish they were weeping uncontrollably.

order.why: Read the reported gathering in the garden before departure.
shortened: When the Blessed Perfection moved into the garden of Hajib Pasha, outside of Bagdad, for twelve days there was a general feast. A great tent was raised in the center of the garden, under which Baha'u'llah received all the callers, the ministers, the theologians, the learned and the prominent leaders of the Community.

order.why: Consider the reported farewell and its spiritual significance.
Keep the account of dignity amid banishment.
Read the departure in its language of spiritual sovereignty.
Retain the paired brief historical notices.
shortened: When Baha'u'llah and His retinue left Baghdad for Constantinople, Muhammad-'Ali was in His company, and continued on with Him to the Land of Mystery, Adrianople.
Baha'u'llah and His retinue then left Baghdad, the "Abode of Peace," for Constantinople, the "City of Islam."

order.why: Hear the announcement of departure.
Read the concise statement of westward movement.
shortened: Say: The Spirit at that time departeth from Iraq and turneth toward a western direction.

order.why: Consider the Nightingale seeking another branch.
shortened: Say: The Bird of Immortality hath taken flight in truth, and thereby have the hearts of them that are near been consumed. Say: The Nightingale of the Spirit hath flown from the branch of Iraq and seeketh another branch, as decreed by the mysteries of destiny in the preserved tablets of holiness.

order.why: Read the Dove of Eternity and the breezes of separation.
Hear the personal remembrance amid departure.
shortened: Thus doth the Dove of Separation remember thee at the time when It taketh flight from Iraq, and this is indeed a grievous sorrow.

order.why: Retain the Tablet’s statement of separation and oppression.
shortened: This is a Tablet wherein are mentioned verses of separation from this poor and wretched servant at the time when He departeth from the region of Iraq by reason of that which the hands of the oppressors have wrought.

order.why: Read the signs of separation within the Book’s imagery.
shortened: This is a Book which speaks with truth, and in it is that which guides people to a wondrous spring, and in it are detailed the gems of knowledge from the presence of One mighty and powerful, and in it are mentioned the signs of separation on the day when the Dove of the Cause shall wing its flight from the branch of Iraq to the holy and luminous Ridvan.

order.why: Hear the call to listen at the moment of departure.
shortened: O people of the Bayan! Hear My call at the time of departure from the shore of Iraq, and be not of the heedless ones.

order.why: Consider the exhortation carried by the departing Dove.
shortened: Thus doth the Dove admonish you and remind you with verses of mighty glory. Say: It counseleth the loved ones at a time when it taketh flight from the branch of Iraq, that perchance the people may arise from the couches of heedlessness.

order.why: Read the flight in relation to divine wisdom.
shortened: Then know thou that this Bird hath taken flight from the branches of Iraq, and this was ordained by the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.

order.why: Turn toward the reported division of practical duties.
shortened: When we left Bagdad for Constantinople as there were a large number of us we had to divide our duties.

order.why: Read the named responsibilities within the travelling party.
shortened: When the Blessed Perfection was exiled from Bagdad, the large number of the believers who followed him, divided the work of the party amongst themselves. For example: Darveesh Sedk Ali and Haji Ebrahim acted as equerries; Astad Mohamad Ali looked after the baggages; Mirza Mohamad Goli supervised the pitching up of the tents and I was - if we may use the Military expression in this connection - a commissary officer and I had to supply the party including the horses etc with food and daily necessities.

order.why: Consider the reported exhaustion and provision of necessities.
shortened: When the Blessed Perfection (Baha'Ullah) was exiled from Bagdad the large number of believers who went with him divided the work of the party among them.

Often, by day or by night we covered a distance of from twenty-five to thirty miles. No sooner would we reach a caravanserai than from sheer fatigue everyone would lie down and go to sleep: utter exhaustion having overtaken everybody they would be unable even to move.

order.why: Keep the reported stages, scarcity, and transport details attributed.
shortened: There were 60 stages from Bagdad to Samson and the trip was made under the most difficult circumstances. It was a time of famine and scarcity of food. We had beside more than 70 people in the party and nearly 30 horses and other animals.

The Blessed Perfection travelled in "Kajavé" but we had a horse for him and sometimes he would ride on it. From Bagdad to the first stage he was on horseback and while in Acca, we had a wonderful white donkey which belonged to him. The name of the donkey was "Barg" - lightening.

order.why: Read the reported difficulty of staying awake in the saddle.
Retain the selected plan to prepare camp ahead of the party.
shortened: When we were travelling from Bagdad toward Constantinople, one day, we thought [to] go ahead of the family, pitch the tent and prepare everything till Baha'u'llah and the rest of the party arrive.

order.why: Keep the reported journey of a particular dervish.
Read the brief remembrance of companions’ hardships.
shortened: From Baghdad to Adrianople, some of the friends like Jinab Aqa Mirza Mahmud and Aqa Mirza Ja'far endured great hardships.

order.why: Preserve the particular recollection of visits before departure.
shortened: He was still in Bagdad when we were exiled to Constantinople and used to call on me almost every week antecedent to our departure.

order.why: Read the account of family and companions made captives.
Reach the sea through the Tablet associated with Samsun.
Read the sea’s oath with its following statement restored from the same source.
shortened: We proceeded until We reached the sea. We sat and heard from its murmuring: "By God! The Beloved of the world has come, and He has appeared through Whose appearance the eyes of the Messengers were consoled."

order.why: Consider the sea and ark as images of sovereignty.
Read the extended account of the voyage, stay, and further departure.
shortened: We preserved it through a power from Us, and protected those who embarked upon it until they reached its shore in the city whose name is renowned among you, if ye be of the knowing ones. And We remained therein for four successive months, as inscribed in preserved and mighty Tablets. Throughout those months none of those who dwelt therein, whether high or low, sought Our company.

We went not unto anyone, nor turned toward any soul, thus manifesting God's sovereignty and His command, and proclaiming God's power and His dominion, until the appointed time of tarrying was fulfilled. Then We departed therefrom and traversed the way until We entered this remote prison.

order.why: Keep the further account of arrival and four months’ residence.
shortened: After traversing all these aforementioned stages, we reached the sea.

From there we took a carriage to the residence assigned by the government. We remained four months in that unillumined city and left there the fruit of the divine Tree and the leaf of the heavenly Lote-Tree.

order.why: Hear the reported question addressed to the ambassador.
shortened: When the Blessed Perfection was in Constantinople He sent a message to Mirza Hossein Khan, the Persian Ambassador, through the then well-known Mirza Safa to this effect: What dost thou expect to do with me?

order.why: Retain the concise statement concerning gatherings and exile.
Read the reported failure of removal to extinguish the Cause.
shortened: As it took one month to go from Tehran to Baghdad, it was thought by the people that all trace of the cause would be lost; on the contrary, the Cause of God became more powerful, his words more widely spread, his proclamation more generally heard and the power of his Cause the stronger; consequently the government decided to send the Blessed Perfection from Baghdad to Constantinople. As Constantinople was a large city and as there were many Persians in the city who traveled freely, this plan also proved fruitless.

order.why: Keep the further reported account of unintended growth.
Consider the widening proclamation through successive banishments.
shortened: And when they strove to banish and expel the manifest light from Iran, the mighty banner was raised in Iraq. And when they engaged in hypocrisy in Iraq, it caused the Ancient Beauty to be exiled to the renowned city, and the mighty drum and the greatest bell were struck in Istanbul.

order.why: Read the reported transformation of grief in retrospect.
Explore the reported reflection on unexpected openings.
shortened: But they thought that if they exiled the Blessed Beauty, this Lamp would be extinguished and the holy fragrances would cease. Yet had this exile not occurred, how would the divine call have arisen in Istanbul? Where would the divine call have become world-embracing in the Holy Land? How would the divine fame have reached East and West? All of these were due to the blessing of that exile.

order.why: Read the journey as signs offered for discernment.
Close with the Sun setting from one horizon and dawning from another.

questions: What does the memory of the rose add to accounts of banishment and political pressure?
How do practical duties and care for companions contribute to the spiritual meaning of the journey?
What differences emerge among recollection, symbolic language, historical explanation, and protest?
How do the passages hold together imposed suffering, dignity, grief, and joy?
What parallels and limits do you see in the comparison with Paul’s account of confinement?
How might the connected subjects of declaration and successive banishments change your understanding of this particular journey?

references.label: 1 · Philippians 1:12–14 · A message spreading through confinement
references.note: Paul describes his confinement as contributing to the spread of the Gospel and to others’ courage in speaking. Compare that retrospective interpretation with the accounts here of exile opening new places to the Bahá’í message. The comparison concerns responses and unexpected consequences; it neither equates the historical circumstances nor justifies persecution.
